items.title: We've been tracking graphics card prices for exactly one year and it's never been worse than this
items.summary: And I don't know where we go from here. Any positive thoughts welcome.
items.body: We first started tracking the prices of individual graphics cards on August 14, 2025, and since then we've checked on an almost weekly cadence (we've got to have holidays, y'know). And it's not been a pretty year. In the interests of full disclosure, the methodology behind this data capture has been to have one editor spend an inordinate amount of their work day tracking down the cheapest available version of each of the current generation of GPUs from Nvidia, AMD, and yes, even Intel. They must be new in-box, so no refurbs or open box sales, and they must be from reputable sellers—no vendors on Amazon called sdfgwegggggwawfdasfsreqwwqeccccawef, in other words. This data captures the very cheapest prices these GPUs were available for throughout the year, but what it doesn't capture is the average price, which has often been much higher. Sometimes there might be a good deal on a particular graphics card, while the rest of the market is significantly more expensive. But our idea was to capture what a reader could spend in a particular week to bag the GPU chipset they wanted. items.title: 'To own a Razer Artisan Keycap is to display one’s allegiance, a mark of belonging within the Cult of Razer' says the PR nonsense behind this $90 coil of snakes
items.summary: It's Medusa-friendly, though.
items.body: "To own a Razer Artisan Keycap is to display one’s allegiance, a mark of belonging within the cult of Razer," says the marketing gumph for the company's first artisan keycap . I've read a lot of ambitious press releases in this job, but that's definitely the strangest sentence I've parsed this year. That being said, I do like the look of the Razer Artisan Keycap - Triple-Headed Snake Edition . Because as the name suggests, it's made up of a twisting coil of snakes. Indiana Jones wouldn't approve, but as for Andy-ana Edser? Aye, it's alright by me. Razer's slippery new keycap is resin-cast, has been individually hand-painted (I'd genuinely enjoy that job), and subjected to a two-stage quality control process that makes sure no dust or bubbles are left on the final product. It's been designed to fit on MX-style, cross-stem switches, so it should be compatible with most keyboards. Even if you haven't bought into the cult of Razer and gone for a competitor's product instead. Which is probably some form of heresy in Razer's eyes, I would imagine. items.title: انتهت المهلة.. تشيلسي يغلق بابه في وجه مانشستر سيتي
items.summary: النادي اللندني كان قد حدد شروطه
items.body: النادي اللندني كان قد حدد شروطه انتهت المهلة التي حددها تشيلسي أمام الأندية الراغبة في التعاقد مع لاعبه الأرجنتيني، إنزو فيرنانديز، مقابل 120 مليون جنيه إسترليني، دون وصول أي عرض رسمي مكتوب من مانشستر سيتي أو أي نادٍ آخر، لتتراجع فرص رحيل لاعب الوسط عن البلوز هذا الصيف. وذكر الصحفي البريطاني، بن جاكوبس، مساء اليوم الجمعة، أن هذه الشروط كانت قد أُبلغت شفهيًا لممثلي فيرنانديز، في مايو الماضي، لتقديمها إلى الأندية الراغبة في ضمه. اقرأ أيضًا مدافع الفراعنة يحط رحاله في الدوري الإيطالي يويفا مصمم على الإطاحة بإنفانتينو.. ومرشحان عربيان لرئاسة الفيفا ويُعد مانشستر سيتي أبرز المهتمين بضم فيرنانديز، خصوصًا مع رغبة مدربه إنزو ماريسكا في العمل مجددًا مع اللاعب الأرجنتيني، الذي سبق أن دربه خلال فترته مع تشيلسي. ولا يزال من الممكن نظريًا أن يتحرك السيتي بعرض بعد انتهاء المهلة، لكن تشيلسي أصبح يتوقع استمرار فيرنانديز معه في موسم 2026-2027، بحسب بن جاكوبس. ويملك اللاعب عقدًا مع النادي اللندني حتى عام 2031. وكان تشيلسي قد تعاقد معه قادمًا من بنفيكا البرتغالي، في يناير 2023، مقابل صفقة بلغت نحو 106.8 مليون جنيه إسترليني.

items.title: The Epic Games Launcher will be available on Linux 'soon' says dev, after it's had a bit of work
items.summary: Another year of Linux PC gaming, perhaps?
items.body: Linux gaming has been rumbling along in the background for some time. However, this seems to be the year it reaches a wider audience, as proper Linux support has become a much-requested feature for many platforms. Next up is the Epic Games Store/Launcher, it seems, as an Epic dev has responded to a user query about Linux support with an emoji saying "soon." The conversation was spotted (and indeed, screenshotted) by Mr_Madafaka on Reddit. "But not for the preview release," says Onepercentnachos on the Epic Games Store Discord community server. "As you can imagine, we need to do more than simply have a build of the launcher that can run natively on Linux." Even some of our own team have made the leap into Linux in 2026 , mostly due to sheer malaise towards Windows 11 and its tiresome ways. Linux is far from a fresh new face in the gaming space, but Microsoft's previously ubiquitous OS seems to be losing ground. Valve is in the process of adding more handheld support to the Linux-based SteamOS , too, and the Steam Deck is extremely popular. items.summary: I think Terraria is a great fit.
items.body: The crowning achievement of a game is no longer player count or Metacritic score, it's actually the number of collabs it can squeeze into its lifecycle—soon every game will collab with each other to make one giant game. I can see it coming. Although that may not be the case for Palworld , even with its current collabs it won't just let any old IP work with the critters-with-guns survival game. (Image credit: Pocketpair) "If it really doesn’t make sense then obviously we would never go ahead with it," the head of publishing and communications, John 'Bucky' Buckley, recently revealed in a social media post (via GamesRadar ). "You guys simply do not realize the sheer number of collabs we've rejected or scrapped for that reason." All I can say to that is good—collabs for the sake of collabs suck. items.summary: "الراقي" أجرى تغييرات عديدة قبل بداية الموسم
items.body: "الراقي" أجرى تغييرات عديدة قبل بداية الموسم واصل نادي الأهلي رحلة إعارة مواهبه الصاعدة إلى أندية دوري روشن السعودي، بالتزامن مع بداية الموسم الكروي الجديد 2026-2027. وأعلن نادي الأهلي، اليوم الجمعة، موافقته على إعارة لاعبه أيمن فلاتة إلى صفوف الفيصلي، الصاعد حديثًا إلى دوري روشن، حتى نهاية الموسم الجديد. فلاتة سيلحق بزميله في الأهلي، لاعب الوسط الصاعد عيد المولد ، والذي سبق أن وافق "الراقي" على إعارته إلى الفيصلي حتى نهاية الموسم أيضًا. تذاكر مباريات دوري روشن السعودي اشترِ تذكرتك الآنَ! وأصبح فلاتة خامس اللاعبين الراحلين عن الأهلي على سبيل الإعارة في الميركاتو الصيفي الحالي، بجانب عيد المولد، وعبدالإله الخيبري المُنتقل إلى الفتح، وياسين الزبيدي ويزن مدني للخلود. وبشكل عام، فقد الأهلي 7 لاعبين خلال الميركاتو الصيفي حتى الآن، يتقدمهم الخماسي المُعار، وكذلك الجناح الجزائري رياض محرز ولاعب الوسط الإيفواري فرانك كيسيه، بالإضافة للمدرب الألماني ماتياس يايسله. وبدأ الأهلي مشواره في دوري روشن السعودي أمس الخميس، من خلال الفوز على الدرعية بهدف نظيف، سجله لاعب الوسط الأرميني إدوارد سبيرتسيان الوافد من كراسنودار الروسي. #الأهلي يوافق على إعارة أيمن فلاتة https://t.co/KbXQVfbjhl — النادي الأهلي السعودي (@ALAHLI_FC) August 14, 2026

items.summary: Performance anxiety.
items.body: Arc System Works can do just about anything, including convincing me to pick up a Marvel-themed 2D anime fighter. Not that I've got anything particularly against either of those things. items.summary: "العالمي" يستعد لمواجهة الفتح

items.body: ليست إصابة.. كشفت مصادر داخل نادي برشلونة عن سر غياب بيدري عن التدريبات الجماعية للفريق، رغم عودته إلى المدينة الرياضية يوم الأربعاء الماضي رفقة بقية اللاعبين الدوليين الإسبان. وأصبح المدرب هانز فليك يمتلك الآن جميع لاعبي الفريق الأول تحت تصرفه، لكن لاعب الوسط القادم من جزر الكناري، البالغ من العمر 23 عامًا، لم يشارك مع المجموعة منذ عودته، مما أثار التساؤلات. وبحسب صحيفة " موندو ديبورتيفو " الإسبانية، فإن الأمر لا يتعلق بإصابة، بل بخطة عودة محددة وُضعت للاعب.  ولفتت الصحيفة إلى أن مسؤول اللياقة البدنية أوصى بأن يبدأ بيدري تحضيراته داخل صالة الألعاب الرياضية خلال الأيام الأولى، بشكل منفصل عن زملائه، بهدف تنظيم حمله البدني بعد فترة التوقف الدولي. وكان ابن مدينة تيجويستي قد نشر قبل انضمامه لتدريبات برشلونة صورًا له وهو يتدرب منفردًا، في إشارة إلى التزامه ببرنامجه الخاص. ومن المنتظر أن يعود بيدري للركض على أرض الملعب يوم السبت المقبل كخطوة تالية في برنامجه، وسط حالة من الاطمئنان التام داخل النادي بشأن حالته، وعدم وجود أي قلق حول غيابه المؤقت عن المران الجماعي.

I couldn't possibly call it a bad gaming mouse, because taste aside, it's a bit of a beast. It's just not a feasible buy for someone only looking for a competitive-level gaming mouse, and that's before mentioning the weight increase that comes with shoving gold inside it. Feeling like it's ripped straight out of Deus Ex: Human Revolution , I think its smattering of blacks and golds looks super clean. items.body: From the archives: This article originally ran in PC Gamer #326 (UK, January 2019). Something I miss when I play digital games is the tactile side of play. It’s why videogames and board games coexist in my life so beautifully. One allows for complexity beyond what a pen-and-paper can track, and the other offers tokens to hold, boards to construct, people to physically turn to as you play. Somewhere in the middle are a wonderful selection of videogames where you feel compelled to take notes. I’m not talking about games which demand you fetch a sheet of paper as part of the experience. These are games where my experience just happens to spill over into the real world as drawings and words. The ones where I decide to keep my thoughts straight by idly jotting down words, phrases, the location of a treasure to come back to or an area to investigate more thoroughly. After a while the odd word or two becomes a page, perhaps even a map. Arrows allow paragraphs to put out little runners, setting down roots in blank spaces and fruiting whole new clusters of notes. items.body: One of the special pleasures in any medieval game is getting to field a trebuchet. In an era where warfare was largely a contest of who can keep people swinging their unfriendliest sticks around the longest before they get hungry enough to leave, there's a sort of giddiness that comes with being the guy who's weaponized the higher art of applied physics to fling half-ton boulders better than any run-of-the-mill onager could ever hope to. Sadly, there have in fact been real human beings who were unfortunate enough to be in the way of those boulders over the years, and as reported earlier this week by Science , researchers have identified a skeleton they believe could very well be the first confirmed trebuchet casualty in the archaeological record. (Image credit: Xbox Games Studios) The skeleton in question is Skeleton 150, one of a number of skeletons dating back to the 1300s that were unearthed during excavations beneath the chapel of Stirling Castle in Scotland in 1997. Skeleton 150 was one of five whose bones bore the evidence—cut marks, puncture wounds, blunt force trauma—of having died violently. items.title: This spy game is a dream come true if you love spending time in character creators
items.summary: And if your character isn't convincing enough, you die.
items.body: Are you someone who spends almost as much time creating your characters as you do playing them in an RPG? Love obsessing over the details of your avatar's facial features, browsing the menu of noses, eyes, ears, and facial hair for ages? Think you're good enough that you could make your character look so much like someone else that you could fool people? Good, because Legion Was Here is a game that spends more time in the character creator than it does anywhere else, and if you can't create a convincing character, you die. In Legion Was Here you're a spy. Scratch that: you're the spy. This game is the opposite of James Bond walking into every undercover situation and saying "Hi, I'm James Bond." You're gifted at stealing someone's identity and impersonating them down to the very finest detail, mimicking them so expertly that their friends, family, and associates will have no idea they're talking to an imposter. At least, that's the idea. Your mission begins on the operating table, where you page through a dossier of information about the person you're going to be replacing. items.title: If you're not paying attention to retro game recompilations, you're missing the most exciting thing in gaming right now
items.summary: Forget all the new games coming out in 2026. Newly shiny old games are where it's at.
items.body: In a few months, Nintendo will release a shiny remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Switch 2. Given its reputation as one of Nintendo's crown jewels, I imagine it will be remarkably faithful to the original, but with new graphics, some tweaks to the controls, and a few other modern touches—like the kinds we've been able to play Ocarina of Time with on PC since 2022 . Ocarina of Time's unofficial PC port Ship of Harkinian , developed by a group dedicated to reverse-engineering the Nintendo 64 game and painstakingly rewriting its code, has a built-in randomizer, accessibility options like text-to-speech, and literally hundreds of enhancements, from autosaving to tunable difficulty to ultrawide to high framerate support. There are options as granular as letting Link unsheathe his sword without attacking and disabling certain graphical effects so that they can be replaced with mods. Speaking of mods: There are hundreds of those , too, letting you use the character models from the 2011 3DS port, make the UI HD, or play as Wario if you're freaky like that. But aside from the sentimental concerns—which, honestly, I don't hold as any less important, there's more to life than money—there is a capitalist argument against the move, too, for both the consumer and the people who make videogames. If Sony ends physical disk sales, Sony decides how much a game on the PlayStation costs, forever. Such is the argument of one Dutch consumer group that's currently suing Sony for their proposed changes, stating last month that "no discs means no second-hand market and no alternative to the PlayStation Store, so from 2028, Sony alone decides what a game costs and even how long you are allowed to use it." At the very least, despite Steam's monolithic popularity, Valve's not capable of forcing anybody to use it. You can still use GOG or Itch.io or… Epic, if you really wanted to. For a few years now, we've heard a lot of overexcitement from the videogame industry that AI is going to let smaller companies make bigger games, that soon you'll be able to generate your own concept art, your own music, your own videogame dialogue —and, of course, the deeply tedious phrase "democratising art".
